per_question.question: Are there quantity limits on prescription drugs under NC Medicaid, and when is prior authorization required for pharmacy claims?
per_question.agent_answer:
I’m going to pull the pharmacy policy sections that address quantity limits and prior authorization criteria, then I’ll check whether there are any amendments affecting those rules.I found the core pharmacy policy: Clinical Coverage Policy 9. Next I’m reading the general pharmacy coverage section plus the quantity-limit and prior-authorization sections so I can answer from the full text rather than snippets.The search result labeled “Policy 9” is actually the NC Medicaid Outpatient Pharmacy policy document. I’ve confirmed it contains sections on quantity/episodic drugs and the PA request process; now I’m pulling the main PA and coverage-limits sections plus amendments so I can answer the substance, not just the process.**Yes — NC Medicaid does impose quantity-related limits on at least some prescription drugs, and prior authorization is required for drugs that fall under NC Medicaid’s pharmacy prior-approval criteria.**

## Short answer

- **Quantity limits:** Yes. The outpatient pharmacy policy expressly refers to **“quantity limitations of episodic drugs”** and to **prior authorization criteria and requirements** for those drugs. It also refers to steps to reduce multiple dispensing fees when drugs are prescribed in limited quantities.  
  **Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Section 5.4.3 — “Quantity and Episodic Drugs” (effective July 15, 2024), [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

- **Prior authorization (PA):** PA is required when the drug is one of NC Medicaid’s **“Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria”** drugs/categories, or when the claim hits PA-related limits in the point-of-sale system. If PA has not been obtained, the POS system returns messages such as **“PA REQ. PRESCRIBER CALL CSC”** or **“CLAIM DENIED. PA LIMITS EXCEEDED.”**  
  **Citations:**  
  - Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Attachment C — “Requesting Prior Authorization for Prescription Drugs” (effective July 15, 2024), [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)  
  - Clinical Coverage Policy 9 — “Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria” (effective July 15, 2024), [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

## What the policy actually says

### 1) Quantity limits
The clearest retrieved language is in **Section 5.4.3**, which states that the policy addresses:

- **“Evaluating the applicability of quantity limitations of episodic drugs”** for beneficiaries who normally get legend medications in specialized packaging;
- **“Prior authorization criteria and requirements”;** and
- **“Actions that minimize the number of dispensing fees for drugs that are prescribed in limited quantities.”**

That confirms NC Medicaid pharmacy policy does use **quantity limitations** at least for **episodic drugs**.  
**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Section 5.4.3 — “Quantity and Episodic Drugs” (effective July 15, 2024), [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

### 2) When PA is required
The retrieved materials do **not** give one universal sentence saying “all drugs require PA in X circumstances.” What they do show is:

- NC Medicaid maintains a list/category set called **“Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria,”** which includes many specific drug classes and products, such as:
  - GLP-1 receptor agonists and combinations
  - Hepatitis C medications
  - Growth hormones
  - PCSK9 inhibitors
  - Opioid analgesics
  - Synagis
  - CGM systems and related supplies
  - various other named products/classes  
  **Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9 — “Pharmacy Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria” (effective July 15, 2024), [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

- The PA request process says the **prescriber** requests PA through NCTracks/CSC, and if PA has not been completed, the pharmacy claim will return:
  - **“PA REQ. PRESCRIBER CALL CSC”** or
  - **“CLAIM DENIED. PA LIMITS EXCEEDED.”**  
  **Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9, Attachment C — “Requesting Prior Authorization for Prescription Drugs” (effective July 15, 2024), [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

So, based on the text I retrieved, **PA is required when the drug is subject to NC Medicaid’s prior-approval criteria or when claim limits trigger a PA edit at POS**.

## Important limitation
I **could not find, in the sections I retrieved, a complete chart of exact quantity caps or a full rule listing every trigger for PA**. The policy clearly establishes that:
- quantity limits exist for some drugs; and
- PA is required for drugs/classes under the **Prior Approval Drugs and Criteria** framework.

But I did **not** retrieve a section that states all exact numeric limits, refill thresholds, or every class-specific trigger. Under your question, that means I should not invent exact limits.

## Amendment status
I checked amendments for this document and the tool identifies the current authoritative document as **Clinical Coverage Policy 9**, effective **July 15, 2024**. I did not find a separate amendment notice to cite for these retrieved sections.  
**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 9 (effective July 15, 2024), [Lock-in Program](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/9-outpatient-pharmacy-program/download?attachment)

## Bottom line
- **Yes, quantity limits exist** under NC Medicaid outpatient pharmacy policy.  
- **PA is required** when a drug falls within NC Medicaid’s **prior approval drug criteria** or when the claim triggers a PA/limit edit in POS.  
- If no PA has been obtained, the pharmacy may receive **“PA REQ. PRESCRIBER CALL CSC”** or **“CLAIM DENIED. PA LIMITS EXCEEDED.”**

If you want, I can do a second pass specifically for either:
1. **exact quantity-limit rules** for retail pharmacy claims, or  
2. **the full list of PA-trigger drug categories and criteria**.
